turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided that, Hale, and when?
You didn't answer my question. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Owen is a great kid. Really bright, one of my favourites.
"One of my favourites." Then why did he find out on his phone in front of his class? Who entered the zero, Hale, and was Owen heard first?
I'm sure this is all just a misunderstanding.
"A misunderstanding." Then withdraw the zero today and put that in writing. If you can't, tell me what you actually have.
So can we agree he's a good student?
Don't manage me, Hale. His average is 91.2, and your zero puts his scholarship at risk with three weeks to the deadline. What do you have, or am I going upstairs?
